derivation: from neuter plural of G3588 (ὁ) and G3568 (νῦν);
def: the things now, i.e. (adverbially) at present

occurrences.text: And now, Lord, behold their threatenings: and grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word,
And now I say unto you, Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought:
And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
